candidates.original_title: Examining the relations between executive function, math, and literacy during the transition to kindergarten: A multi-analytic approach
candidates.description: Bidirectional associations between executive function and math/literacy achievement from preschool to kindergarten
candidates.citation_sentence: The goal of the current study was to conduct a conceptual replication of the reciprocal associations between executive function and academic achievement reported in Schmitt et al. (2017, https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000193).
candidates.notes: Pathways sample (N=279). Failed to replicate bidirectional EF–achievement associations; found only unidirectional EF → math and EF → literacy paths.

candidates.original_title: Examining the relations between executive function, math, and literacy during the transition to kindergarten: A multi-analytic approach
candidates.description: The original study claimed that executive function prospectively predicted math achievement, but not literacy achievement, across kindergarten, within a broader pattern of reciprocal associations between executive function and academic achievement.
candidates.citation_sentence: The goal of the current study was to conduct a conceptual replication of Schmitt et al. (2017, https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000193).
candidates.notes: Pathways sample; executive function predicted subsequent math and literacy achievement, but math and literacy did not predict executive function, so the overall replication evidence was mixed.

candidates.original_title: Examining the relations between executive function, math, and literacy during the transition to kindergarten: A multi-analytic approach
candidates.description: The original study claimed bidirectional associations between executive function and math achievement, as well as associations between executive function and literacy achievement, across the transition from preschool to kindergarten, with executive function prospectively predicting math achievement across kindergarten.
candidates.citation_sentence: The goal of the current study was to conduct a conceptual replication of Schmitt et al. (2017, https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000193).
candidates.notes: STAR sample; the replication found executive function predicted subsequent math achievement but did not reproduce the original bidirectional pattern. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
